_comment: Hybrid sprite manifest — maps IDs to external sprite sheet paths. ⚠️ REGISTERING ART HERE DOES NOT MAKE IT RENDER. Measured 2026-09-11: most sections have NO reader in src/ at all. HybridSpriteLoader:88-90 looks entries up by key for 'sheets', 'monster_sheets' and 'battle_effects', and TileSheetManifest:31 reads 'tile_sheets' — a DIFFERENT consumer, not the sprite loader. Every other family is resolved by FILENAME CONVENTION through a composed path and never consults its section — jobs via jobs/<job_id>/<anim>.png, NPCs via npcs/<archetype>/overworld.png, overworld monsters via monsters/overworld/<monster_id>.png (RoamingMonster / MasteriteEncounter). So: putting the file at the conventional path is what makes art RENDER; the entry here is what makes it ATTRIBUTED — the tier/provenance record the artist-collab rules in CLAUDE.md require, and what tools/update_artist_ledger.py and the audit tests read. Both matter, for different reasons. If you registered art and nothing appears on screen, check the PATH against the loader's convention, not this file. (weapon_sheets currently has neither a key reader nor a path consumer — weapons render procedurally via weapon_id through SnesPartySprites; see its entries.)

cave_rat.source: artist aseprite drop 2026-08-20 — Game graphics - Characters/enemies/Rat animations.aseprite (artist tags Idle 0-3, Atk 4-9; 2.25x nearest-neighbor, whole canvas scaled once with ONE shared offset so the artist's inter-frame registration is preserved. Scale = min(match-reference-height, fit-widest-frame) per the skeleton precedent: content 252x144 in a 256 frame (skeleton is 250x185), feet seated at y=217 — exactly where the T1 sheet had them. A first pass used a flat 2x and came out under convention at 224x128; struktured had already rejected that on the skeleton ("way too small, you need like 2.5x")). HORIZONTALLY FLIPPED on ingest: the artist drew this one facing LEFT, and monsters face RIGHT (struktured 2026-08-27); the artist's own goblin faces right, this source is the outlier. The artist authored NO hit and NO dead — hit -> frame 4 is the ATTACK WINDUP and dead -> frame 0 is a plain IDLE, both REUSED placeholders exactly as the goblin does, so the rat visibly neither flinches nor falls. Dedicated hit/dead frames are an ARTIST ask. Previous T1 sheet preserved at cave_rat.pre_artist.png. ⚠️ THE FLIP IS BAKED INTO THE PIXELS AND THAT IS ONLY CORRECT AT frame_height > 128. BattleScene infers artist-monster status from frame height alone (ENEMY_SMALL_FRAME_THRESHOLD=128, BattleScene.gd:46) and sets BOTH a 2.5x size bump AND sprite.flip_h from it. At 256 this sheet gets neither, which is why the baked flip renders correctly. RE-EXPORTING THIS AT 128 WOULD DOUBLE-FLIP IT — engine flip on top of the baked one — and the rat would face away from the party with nothing red. Either keep 256 with the flip baked (current, matches skeleton/wolf/spider), or drop to 128 AND remove the --flip. The repo runs both conventions among T2 monsters: 128 for bat/goblin/slime/mordaine/the_calibrant, 256 for skeleton/wolf/spider/imp and this one.

_field_provenance._why: Fields with NO runtime reader. The rule this implements (cowir-music/cowir-main, 2026-09-16): an authored key must be READ by the runtime or DECLARED inert with a note naming who holds it — you cannot silence it green, only explain it green. test_a_manifest_field_is_read_or_declared reds on a field that is neither.
_field_provenance.generator: which tool wrote the sheet. Read across tools/ and by a human deciding whether an AI regen may touch it — never by the game.
_field_provenance._note: prose for the next reader of this file. Never parsed.
_field_provenance.flip_h_reason: why a sheet's flip_h was set against the frame-size convention. The DECISION is flip_h, which the loader reads; this records the argument.
_field_provenance.bust_rect_reason: why a monster sheet declares its cutscene bust instead of the measured figure square, and which landmarks it was read from. The DECISION is bust_rect, which HybridSpriteLoader.declared_bust_rect reads; this records the argument (cowir-sprites).
_field_provenance.derived_from: the village whose _get_cliff_palette() a world atlas was recoloured from. Read by test_a_village_palette_is_not_silently_overridden, not by src/ — it is the evidence that an override is a no-op in hue.
_field_provenance.derived_palette: the exact colours used at generation time. Its job is to EXPIRE: if the village's colours change, the guard reds and the atlas is stale.
_field_provenance.tier: the artist-first pipeline tier (T0 procedural / T1 AI / T2 artist draft / T3 artist final) from CLAUDE.md. Authored on every entry; read across tools/ (24 scripts at last sweep — derive it, do not trust this sentence to age) and by the artist deciding what an AI regen may touch — never by src/. The "tier" hits in src/ are autogrind's grind tier and ShopScene's spell tier, different data under the same name.
_field_provenance.source: how the sheet was produced — model, prompt or ingest run. Provenance for the artist ledger and for a human judging whether a sheet may be regenerated. The "source" hits in src/ are RuleComposer's and AbilityVFX's own provenance strings, not this field.
_field_provenance.drawn_for: prop_art interior patterns (counter, shelf, hearth): the layout cells [x, y] a ROLLED pattern was cut for, so its piece lands whole where the room samples it (x mod cols, y mod rows). No runtime reads it: the room samples by position alone. Written by tools/gen_interior_pieces.py --deploy (DRAWN_FOR); held by test_a_shop_is_drawn_from_its_pieces, which reds when a layout block no longer starts at a cell its art was rolled for. Owner: cowir-sprites.

_section_provenance._why: Whole SECTIONS with no runtime reader. A FIELD census cannot see these: every key in an unconsumed section is individually dead, and a section whose fields are all read ELSEWHERE is invisible entirely — `frame_width` is read by the battle sheet loader, so a field census passes over a section nothing opens. Derived, not listed: a section is READ when its quoted name appears in comment-stripped src/.
_section_provenance.weapon_sheets: 4 weapon sheets — ONE tagged T2_artist_draft (iron_sword), THREE tagged T1 (bronze_sword, flame_sword, ice_blade) — (10 PNGs, 44 KB of art / 52 KB with .import sidecars, all present and imported) for a compositing feature that does not exist: no file in src/ names weapon_sheets or assets/sprites/weapons. The note on each entry says "Compose over body animations" — the art is ready and the code was never written. DECLARED rather than excluded from export, because CLAUDE.md's artist-first rule makes what ships a visible decision and quietly dropping artist work from the build is the opposite of it. Wire it or retire it is struktured's call; 44 KB is not a payload argument. CORRECTED 2026-09-18: this note said all FOUR were tagged T2_artist_draft; only iron_sword is. The error direction is attribution INFLATION — it credits the artist for three AI-generated sheets, which is the opposite of the usual artist-first concern and is the half CLAUDE.md principle 5 cares about (the artist always knows what is AI vs hand-drawn). The DATA is right and the note was wrong: tools/audit_sprite_tiers.py now walks weapon_sheets (it read three hardcoded sections until 2026-09-18) and examined all three T1 entries against git, finding no provable artist pixels in any. Note also that T2_artist_draft is not a value in CLAUDE.md's tier table; artist_guard.tier_refusal refuses any tier it does not recognise, so the spelling is safe rather than a fail-open. This note had been audited twice for SIZE and never once for TIER. CORRECTED 2026-09-16: this note said 132 KB twice; the real figure is 44 KB of PNG (52 KB counting .import sidecars, 20 files). The 132 was never a different basis, just wrong, and it had been repeated to struktured several times as the size of the decision. Re-verified the same day with `command grep -raF -f <the 10 declared paths>` (real GNU, not the session shim that silently skips gitignored subtrees) plus a data/ control returning 10: the zero-reference claim HOLDS in both forms, by section name and by exact asset path, and `weapons` appears in no export exclude_filter, so they do ship.
_section_provenance.npc_sheets: SIX conversational NPC sheets, 1326 KB, tier T1, all present and imported: 2048x256, EIGHT 256px frames animating idle / talk / gesture / react. Nothing in src/ builds `assets/sprites/npcs/<name>.png` — the only path forms are `<archetype>/overworld.png` and `<archetype>_<world>/overworld.png`, which are DIRECTORIES. bram, marta, scholar_milo and elder_theron have a live twin there, so those CHARACTERS ship and the talking art does not; elder_theron's is the largest of the six and he is the first NPC in the game. ⛔ ONE DIRECTORY, TWO MEANINGS: a flat `<name>.png` is a talking sheet and `<name>/overworld.png` is a walk sheet, and nothing in the tree says which is which — CutsceneDialogue:1271 records a lane having to correct a portrait registered against the directory form believing it was portrait art. Declared rather than dropped from the export: wire it or retire it is struktured's, and 1.3 MB is not the argument either way.
_section_provenance.party_sheets: EMPTY — zero entries, and no reader. It has never held anything in this tree. Kept rather than deleted because an empty authored section is a decision someone may have been part-way through, and deleting authored structure is not a guard's call; recorded so the next reader knows it is empty on purpose rather than by accident.
_section_provenance.ability_icons: A LEDGER, NOT A ROUTE: AbilityIcons resolves an icon by path convention (DIR + key + .png) and never opens the manifest, exactly like overworld_npc_sheets. The entry exists so the artist-first tooling and the artist can see these 22 icons are T1 procedural placeholders, replaceable file by file. A zero reader here does NOT mean unreachable art.

_field_indirect_readers._why: Fields the census cannot see as READ because the key is supplied by a VARIABLE rather than a literal, so no get("key") appears anywhere. Recorded so a zero here is never mistaken for an unwired promise — the opposite error to _field_provenance's.
_field_indirect_readers.cliff: READ. TileSheetManifest.region(key, section, name) takes the section as a PARAMETER; EnvironmentTileSets passes "cliff" at its _art_or call sites for the edge and face tiles. The literal lives in the caller, which is not a file that parses the manifest.
_field_indirect_readers.overlay: READ, same path: EnvironmentTileSets passes "overlay" to TileSheetManifest.region(key, section, name) for the fringe tiles, so the literal lives in the caller rather than in a file that parses the manifest.
_field_indirect_readers.tiles: READ, same path as cliff/overlay: BaseTileGenerator._artist_tile passes "tiles" to TileSheetManifest.region(key, section, name) for terrain tiles named by TileType (e.g. FOREST, FOREST:1), so the literal lives in the caller rather than in a file that parses the manifest. test_a_tree_is_drawn_not_painted reads it back.
